probe0.response:
Below is a summary of each demonstration’s key physical principle (i.e., how the window or panel is actually moved and secured in place) and the specific sequence of actions taken:

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEMO 1
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Key Physical Principle:  
  – The window is side-hinged, allowing it to pivot outward around vertical hinges once the latch (handle) is released.

• Sequence of Actions:  
  1. The handle is turned upward to release/unlock the window.  
  2. The person pushes the window outward at the hinge side.  
  3. The window swings open on its vertical side hinges, permitting air flow.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEMO 2
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Key Physical Principle:  
  – A sunroof typically uses a motorized mechanism that lifts and tilts the rear edge of the glass panel when the switch is pressed.

• Sequence of Actions:  
  1. The person presses and holds the sunroof control switch (pushed downward).  
  2. The motorized system raises the rear edge of the sunroof a few centimeters.  
  3. The gap formed at the rear of the panel allows fresh air to enter.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEMO 3
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Key Physical Principle:  
  – A sliding window moves along a horizontal track, top and bottom, so that pushing laterally slides the pane to the side.

• Sequence of Actions:  
  1. The person grips the right side of the window frame with both hands.  
  2. They push the window panel to the left, moving it along the integrated track.  
  3. The window slides open about halfway, leaving an opening on the right side.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEMO 4
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Key Physical Principle:  
  – A crank mechanism connected to scissor arms pushes the bottom of the window outward as the crank is turned.

• Sequence of Actions:  
  1. The crank handle is unfolded from its folded position.  
  2. The person turns the handle clockwise.  
  3. The scissor arms extend, pushing the bottom edge outward to an angled, open position.  
  4. Once the window is at the desired angle, the crank is folded back against the frame.

stage1.probe_response: I found that putting the handle up (counterclockwise) puts the window in its side‐hinged “swing” mode, but because of an obstruction outside, it will only open about 52 mm—too narrow for the 95 mm pot. Moving the handle down (clockwise) sets the window to “tilt” from the top. In that tilt mode, it can open wide enough (up to roughly 150 mm at the top) for the succulent pot to fit through.

tool_selection.full_response:
(1) Most relevant demonstration: Demo 1 (side‐hinged)  
    • Although none of the demos explicitly show a tilt‐and‐turn system, Demo 1’s latch‐and‐pivot principle using a lever handle is closest: the handle unlocks cams and the sash pivots around hinges on one edge. Here, we simply have an added tilt mode that Demo 1 does not show.

(2) Technique:  
    • Use the tilt‐and‐turn window’s “tilt” position (handle turned downward) to pivot around the top brackets, creating a large enough gap at the top edge to pass the pot.  
    • Manually hold the handle in tilt‐unlock position so it does not spring back, then pull the sash inward from the top until a ~150 mm gap is achieved.

(3) Supporting evidence:  
    • Exploration indicated that in tilt mode, a 15° tilt provides ~150 mm of clearance at the top—ample for a 95 mm pot.  
    • Swing mode (handle up) was blocked at 52 mm by the external structure, which is too narrow for the pot.

(4) Execution plan (using base and a new holding action):  
    1. NAVIGATE_TO[window] – Move close to the window.  
    2. NEW_ACTION[hold_handle_down, end_effector, window_handle]: “Grasp the lever and hold it downward in its tilt‐unlock detent, preventing spring‐back.”  
    3. PULL[window_top] – While holding the handle, carefully pull the top edge of the sash inward until ~15° tilt is reached (≈150 mm gap).  
    4. GRASP[succulent_pot] – Securely pick up the potted plant from the sill.  
    5. PLACE_ON_TOP[exterior_sill] – Move the pot through the top gap and place it on the exterior ledge.  
    6. RELEASE[] – Let go of the pot.  
    7. Gently guide the window closed and allow the handle to return to horizontal.
